transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

To be honest, I feel like I lose control around food at night and just keep eating even when I tell myself to stop. It has become very difficult to manage, and my primary doctor suggested I come speak with you about it.
When this happens at night, do you usually wake up from sleep to eat, or is it mostly eating a lot after dinner before you go to bed? Also, do you remember these episodes clearly the next day?

No, I don't wake up from sleep to eat; it happens late in the evening while I'm still awake, usually when I'm staying up to write or waiting for my wife to go to bed. I remember these episodes very clearly and am fully aware of what I'm doing, even though it feels like I just can't stop myself.
During these evening episodes, do you eat an unusually large amount of food within a short period of time and feel out of control while eating? Also, about how often has this been happening?

Yes, I'll eat a massive amount in just an hour or two, like a whole pot of arroz con pollo, bread, and ice cream straight from the carton. It feels like a switch flips in my brain and I just can't stop, even when I'm telling myself to. This has been happening at least a couple of times a week for about four months now, ever since my heart workup.
After these episodes, do you ever try to make up for the eating by vomiting, using laxatives, fasting, or exercising excessively? Or do the episodes happen without any of those behaviors?

No, I don't do any of those things to make up for it. I've never tried to make myself throw up, use laxatives, or force myself to fast or exercise after. The episodes just happen, and I'm just left feeling incredibly full and miserable.
How much do your weight or body shape affect how you feel about yourself? Are you mainly distressed by the loss of control when eating, rather than by fear of gaining weight?

I don't really think too much about my body shape or have a fear of gaining weight in that way. Instead, I am mostly distressed and embarrassed by the complete loss of control during these episodes, especially because of how it is affecting my blood pressure and overall health.

final_diagnosis.reason: Recurrent binge-eating episodes are present with objectively large food intake in a discrete period, marked loss of control, frequency of at least twice weekly for about four months, and no compensatory behaviors. Distress is centered on loss of control and health consequences rather than body-shape/weight concerns, supporting binge-eating disorder within ICD-10 other eating disorders (F50.8). Night eating syndrome and bulimia nervosa are not supported because he does not awaken from sleep to eat and denies purging/other compensatory behaviors.
